figures.applies: Panama; the State's report (the Civil and Family Codes' own texts not read).

sources.said: Such changes are possible only after the age of majority (18) has been reached.

figures.finding: The Constitution (art. 70) bars employing minors under fourteen save as the law excepts; the Labour Code (art. 117) bars employing those under fourteen and fifteen-year-olds who have not finished primary school; Panama declared fourteen as its minimum age under ILO Convention 138.

sources.said: The constitutional provision prohibiting the employment of minors under 14 continues to be in force save for exceptions stipulated by the law (article 70 of the Constitution).
Labour Code article 117, which prohibits the employment of persons under 14 and of 15- year olds who have not completed primary education;
Panama duly filed an exception stating that the country's minimum age for admission to employment is 14.

sources.title: Panama: combined third and fourth periodic reports, CRC/C/PAN/3-4 (2009, issued 27 January 2011)
sources.said: Such changes are possible only after the age of majority (18) has been reached. … The constitutional provision prohibiting the employment of minors under 14 continues to be in force save for exceptions stipulated by the law (article 70 of the Constitution). … Labour Code article 117, which prohibits the employment of persons under 14 and of 15- year olds who have not completed primary education; … Panama duly filed an exception stating that the country's minimum age for admission to employment is 14.
